state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The student went wrong in assuming that changing all values by the same proportion would not change the range. To correct this misunderstanding, remember that changing all values by the same proportion will indeed affect the range. Keep in mind that the range is determined by the difference between the highest and lowest values.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get that the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values. So if you change all the heights by the same proportion, like cutting them in half, it would change the highest and lowest values too, right? But I'm still confused about how adding the same amount, like 3 cm, affects the range. Can you explain that part again?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: When you add the same amount, like 3 cm, to each height, it shifts all the values upward by the same amount. This means the highest and lowest values will also increase by 3 cm, changing the range accordingly. Remember, the range is still determined by the difference between the highest and lowest values.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get it a bit better now. So if I add 3 cm to all the heights, the highest and lowest both go up by 3 cm, which changes the range. But what if I added a different number to each height instead of the same amount? Would that change the range differently?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher directly tells the student incorrect information (that adding 3cm changes the range, when it actually doesn't), fails to engage the student in reasoning through examples, and the student remains confused throughout, even developing new misconceptions by Turn 4.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides some direct corrective feedback but fails to show explicit worked steps with actual calculations using the given plant heights, and the feedback in Turn 3 is actually incorrect (adding the same amount to all values does not change the range), which undermines the rule-based approach.
